text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Asked whether disturbances in neighbouring countries can spill over to Macedonia, ambassadors of United States, Germany, France, Russia, Bulgaria, Turkey and OSCE say no because local economic and political situation is different. But newspaper concludes that turbulent situation in Bulgaria, Greece, Serbia and Albania can influence events in Macedonia.
- U.S. Ambassador Christopher Hill says reasons for protests in Albania, Serbia and Bulgaria vary and there is no causen to expect them to spill over the border.
- Russian Ambassador Pjotr Dobroserdev said: "A deepening of the crisis in neighbouring countries can seriously damage stability in the whole region."
- Christian Faber Roth, the OSCE ambassador, said the events in neighbouring countries should remind Macedonian politicians of the "necessity for transparent politics".
- German Ambassador Klaus Schremeier said German investments in Macedonia this year will prevent unrest.
- Turkish Ambassador Unal Marshali said the Dayton peace agreement is "a chance for the region. Only cooperation between all the countries in the region can prevent destabilization."
- Bulgarian Ambassador Angel Dimitrov said the stability of Macedonia depends on its "capacity to resolve internal problems and skills to build bridges with its neighbours".
- French Ambassador Jacques Huntzinger said events in neighbouring countries had no direct effect on Macedonia although they influence stability in the whole region.
- Leader of the Democratic Party Peter Gosev to be new president of the United Liberal and Democratic Parties.
- Socialist Party leader Ljubisav Ivanov blames his ministers in government for "creating factions in the Socialist party and enjoying government armchairs too much".

- Macedonian and Croatian foreign ministers Ljubomir Frckoski and Mate Granic signed consular convention in Zagreb on Tuesday. The regional South European Cooperation Initative (SECI) and the situation in the Balkans were discussed. The two sides share stands on almost all issues.
- Yugoslav and Macedonian experts to discuss mutual cancellation of road tolls and entry taxes. Macedonia considers prices in Yugoslavia to be too high.
- Macedonian Development Minister Abdulmenaf Bedjeti to attend agenda committee of SECI initative in Geneva Thursday.
